title: Prometheus Keeps Running Out of Memory
intro: Prometheus has been OOM-killed three times today, each time a few hours after restart. Its memory graph climbs steadily until it dies. Nothing changed in Prometheus's own config.

steps.prompt: Check how many active time series Prometheus is tracking.
steps.hint: Memory usage scales roughly with the number of active series.

steps.prompt: 8.4 million series is enormous for this environment. Find which metric names have the most series.
steps.hint: One metric is responsible for almost all of it.

steps.prompt: Check the TSDB status API to see which LABEL has the most distinct values.
steps.hint: Look for a label with millions of distinct values.

steps.prompt: Someone added a 'user_id' label to http_requests_total — every user creates a brand new time series. Find when that code shipped.
steps.fake_output: 7d8e9f0 feat: per-user request metrics for analytics dashboard
steps.hint: git log -S finds the commit that added or removed a string.

resolution: A well-intentioned change added user_id as a label on http_requests_total. In Prometheus, every unique combination of label values is a separate time series held in memory, so millions of users meant millions of new series — a 'cardinality explosion'. Memory grew until the OOM killer stepped in, and restarts just replayed the same growth. The fix: remove the user_id label (per-user analytics belongs in logs or an analytics database, not metrics), then drop existing series with a metric_relabel_configs rule while the code fix rolls out. Rule of thumb: labels should have small, bounded sets of values — status code, method, route template — never user IDs, emails, request IDs, or raw URLs. Alerting on prometheus_tsdb_head_series growth catches this in hours instead of after three crashes.
